items.title: Home-managed complications are invisible in hospital data
items.whyItMatters: Only six of 38 studies counted community-managed events (claim c4); a hospital-only cohort would undercount and bias comparisons between agencies.
items.opportunity: Seek the agency's visit notes for the cohort years, and state the undercount if they are not shared.

items.title: No local incidence by line type and care arrangement
items.whyItMatters: The service knows the 41 emergency visits but not the denominator or who is affected.
items.opportunity: Link the 1,870 OPAT episodes to emergency visits and line records to estimate rates per 1,000 catheter days.

items.title: Why patients delay reporting
items.whyItMatters: Delayed reporting (claim c5) cannot be seen in records and may drive late presentations.
items.opportunity: Interview patients and carers sampled from high- and low-complication groups.

items.title: Patients living alone and those with limited English
items.whyItMatters: Patients living alone had more unplanned returns in a similar service, and teaching by leaflet fails those who cannot read it easily.
items.opportunity: Record living arrangement and interpreter need in the cohort and include these patients in the interview sample.

items.title: Confounding by line choice
items.whyItMatters: Clinicians choose midlines for shorter, simpler courses, so crude comparisons of line types mislead.
items.opportunity: Adjust for antibiotic, planned duration and indication, and interpret line type as a secondary contrast.

errorsFound: The need counts 41 emergency visits as the size of the problem; without agency notes the true number of complications is higher and unknown.
reevaluation: The gaps favour a record-based quantitative strand followed by interviews, with the agency's notes as the missing piece that decides how complete the count can be.
summary: Five gaps; home-managed complications and the missing local denominator are high severity.
